subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should `sessions_spawn(runtime: "acp")` gain a first-class OpenClaw skill-context contract, and which selection, redaction, prompt-layer, audit, and resume semantics are allowed?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior crosses ACP session state, external harness prompts, local skill privacy, and Codex/native skill contracts, so automation should not choose the permanent API or default policy.

options.title: Explicit-only contract first
options.body: Add a narrow `skills: string[]` ACP spawn contract with redaction, source/version metadata, audit events, and tests, while deferring `auto` and default skill sets.

options.title: Full selector contract now
options.body: Design explicit, default, and automatic relevance modes together, accepting a larger config/API and observability surface before implementation.

options.title: Defer core injection
options.body: Keep ACP children isolated from OpenClaw-rendered skill content for now and steer users to harness-native skills, MCP bridges, or plugin workflows.

recommendation.title: Explicit-only contract first
recommendation.body: Add a narrow `skills: string[]` ACP spawn contract with redaction, source/version metadata, audit events, and tests, while deferring `auto` and default skill sets.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the ACP runtime/control-plane and `sessions_spawn(runtime: "acp")` feature this decision would extend.
